display.title: Episode 212: Chaya Malka's Esrog and The Ten Wedding Gifts, Chapter 3
display.summary_short: On his mother's yahrzeit, Uncle Yossi tells how she shared her father's esrog with friends as a girl; then the newlyweds of 'The Ten Wedding Gifts' take in a lost child during a blizzard.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 2 Adar 5746, the yahrzeit of Uncle Yossi's mother, Chaya Malka. He describes her life of Torah, mitzvos and helping others come closer to Yiddishkeit, and tells a story from her childhood in Rhode Island. On Hoshana Rabbah, seven-year-old Chaya Malka tearfully asked to borrow her father's lulav and esrog so that friends without one could make the brachah. Her father agreed but warned her to guard the pitum. After visiting all her friends she dropped the esrog and the pitum broke; a kindly tailor pinned it back with a long needle. She told her father the truth, and he laughed: the esrog was now unfit, but it was the last day it was needed. Uncle Yossi says she was already a soldier in Hashem's army, and everyone says the Shema in her memory. After the Hakochainik march, a fifth-grade Beis Rivkah student leads the Shema. 'The Ten Wedding Gifts' continues: months after the wedding, during a fierce blizzard, Avraham and Sarah take in a lost, freezing boy from a mansion beyond the forest, warm him by the fire and put him to bed, to be continued. A listener then wins the Mitzvah Time phone quiz on honoring holy books.
display.lesson: Help others do mitzvos, like a young girl who shared her father's esrog; and kindness to a stranger in need is never forgotten by Hashem.
